reviewerRole: Separate trusted evaluator agent; not the dispatcher author. No repair implementation performed.
scope: durable finalized selection before independent adjudication
all-planned missing and failed episode denominators
cancellation and dead-owner recovery without automatic retry
runtime plus adjudication usage and prospective aggregate allowances
durable budget grant, partial-charge retention and unknown billing holds
private durable state paths and stale callback rejection

resolvedControls.issue: Inconsistent aggregate verdicts could claim correctness with no checks or failed checks.
resolvedControls.resolution: Strict outcome, nonempty scored-check counts, passed counts, infrastructure-error and completion invariants.
resolvedControls.proof: Seven independent malformed-verdict controls reject while retaining the planned episode.

resolvedControls.issue: Durable database opening did not require a private owned parent or reject ancestor/sidecar symlinks.
resolvedControls.resolution: Owned private final directory; regular owned database and SQLite sidecars; ancestor symlinks rejected.
resolvedControls.proof: Independent parent-symlink, nonprivate-parent and sidecar-symlink controls pass.

resolvedControls.issue: Execution callbacks remained usable after finalized selection, allowing discarded late usage.
resolvedControls.resolution: Owner, executing phase, cancellation and abort checks precede one atomic usage/operation write.
resolvedControls.proof: Independent late callback rejection preserves frozen usage and operation handles.

resolvedControls.issue: Known CPU usage could become unknown then regress to a lower known value.
resolvedControls.resolution: Positive known cumulative CPU/cost cannot become null or decrease.
resolvedControls.proof: Independent 20-to-null-to-1 CPU control terminates without adjudication.

resolvedControls.issue: Deadline expiration was reported as user cancellation.
resolvedControls.resolution: Deadline abort reason is retained as episode_timeout.
resolvedControls.proof: Independent deterministic timer control distinguishes timeout from cancel.

resolvedControls.issue: Caller mutation could change transport settings after binding.
resolvedControls.resolution: Constructor snapshots transport methods and configuration, including a copied rate-bound object.
resolvedControls.proof: Independent mode/model/policy/callback mutation control and author nested-bound control pass.

accountingObservations: An unknown final bill retains the unused reservation and blocks further paid dispatch; a second ledger connection sees the same partial charge and hold.
Measured adjudication overrun is retained; ledger freezes further spending and analysis suppresses matched-budget claims.
All 72 pilot and 270 final planned positions are retained in synthetic grid tests, including unsuccessful rows; those synthetic rows are rejected by scored analysis.
Finalized selection is persisted and read back before the distinct adjudication callback; executor input has no oracle identity or adjudicator callback.

proofBoundary.liveControlBranch: Some unit tests exercise accounting/readiness branches using invented approvals and injected inert callbacks. These are unit records, not real-provider evidence; temporary databases are removed.
limitations: This review does not establish a calibrated production experiment executor, verified provider rate ceilings, credentials or real billing.
Injected trusted transports still attest real execution and usage; interfaces and source digests are not external execution proof.
External operation cancellation and subsequent billing reconciliation require the trusted provider integration; retaining a handle does not prove remote termination.
Recovery tests use local process death and PID liveness. PID reuse may conservatively leave a stale episode held rather than recover it.
These deterministic controls and source review do not establish general fault tolerance or benchmark effectiveness.
